Select a mode to check this device for it. Switching is only possible when its required checks pass.
The operating mode cannot be changed while a backup or restore is in progress, because the running job would lose access to the commands it is using. Wait for it to finish or cancel it first.
Waiting for the checks of this mode to finish.
A required check failed, so this mode cannot be used yet. Fix the items above and re-run the checks.
Not available while a backup or restore is running.
DFTB will change from %1$s to %2$s. This is what changes:
New backups, restores and scheduled runs use the new mode from now on. Your profiles, destinations and existing backups are not changed.
Partition images, TWRP-style backups and partition restores need root and will no longer run.
Private app data and Android/data folders can no longer be read or restored; profiles that include them will skip or fail those items.
Shizuku must be running for every backup. It stops after each reboot unless it is started again, and scheduled backups fail while it is not running.
Your root manager will ask to give DFTB superuser access. Allow it permanently so scheduled backups can run unattended.
The companion module must stay installed and enabled in your root manager for the system-wide tools and the boot service.
The companion module stays installed until you remove it in your root manager. DFTB stops mirroring its reboot-resume journal to it.
Some checks for this mode warned or failed. Features that depend on them may not work until they are fixed.
Ask Shizuku to authorize DFTB. The Shizuku service must be running.
See which partitions, apps and folders this mode can reach on this device.
rclone and BusyBox are not bundled in this build yet, so a module built now contains only the tools this device\'s build ships. The result lists exactly what was included and what is missing.
No module file could be produced. The technical details below explain why.

Every backup encrypted with this key becomes permanently unrecoverable, on every destination.
There is no other copy: the key exists only in this device\'s vault, and nobody, including the DFTB developers, can recreate it.
Restoring or verifying those backups will fail from now on.
I understand that backups encrypted with this key will be lost forever.

The trusted-servers file is unreadable or damaged. SSH connections are refused until it is fixed, to protect against impostor servers.
A server presenting a different key is always refused. Forget a server only if you know its key was changed on purpose.
The pinned key of %1$s will be removed.
The next connection trusts whatever key the server presents and pins it again.
If someone is impersonating the server at that moment, DFTB would trust them. Check the new fingerprint with the server\'s administrator.
